origin.description:
file_copy() copies files.

link_copy() creates a new link pointing to the same location as the previous link.

dir_copy() copies the directory recursively at the new location.
origin.usage:
file_copy(path, new_path, overwrite = FALSE)

dir_copy(path, new_path, overwrite = FALSE)

link_copy(path, new_path, overwrite = FALSE)

arguments.name: path
arguments.text: A character vector of one or more paths.

arguments.name: new_path
arguments.text: A character vector of paths to the new locations.

arguments.name: overwrite
arguments.text:
Overwrite files if they exist. If this is FALSE and the
file exists an error will be thrown.

origin.details:
The behavior of dir_copy() differs slightly than that of file.copy() when
overwrite = TRUE. The directory will always be copied to new_path, even
if the name differs from the basename of path.
origin.example:
.old_wd <- setwd(tempdir())
file_create("foo")
file_copy("foo", "bar")
try(file_copy("foo", "bar"))
file_copy("foo", "bar", overwrite = TRUE)
file_delete(c("foo", "bar"))

dir_create("foo")
# Create a directory and put a few files in it
files <- file_create(c("foo/bar", "foo/baz"))
file_exists(files)

# Copy the directory
dir_copy("foo", "foo2")
file_exists(path("foo2", path_file(files)))

# Create a link to the directory
link_create(path_abs("foo"), "loo")
link_path("loo")
link_copy("loo", "loo2")
link_path("loo2")

# Cleanup
dir_delete(c("foo", "foo2"))
link_delete(c("loo", "loo2"))
setwd(.old_wd)

link_copy() creates a new link pointing to the same location as the previous link.

dir_copy() copies the directory recursively at the new location.
translation.usage:
file_copy(path, new_path, overwrite = FALSE)

dir_copy(path, new_path, overwrite = FALSE)

link_copy(path, new_path, overwrite = FALSE)

arguments.name: path
arguments.text: A character vector of one or more paths.

arguments.name: overwrite
arguments.text:
Overwrite files if they exist. If this is FALSE and the

translation.details:
The behavior of dir_copy() differs slightly than that of file.copy() when
overwrite = TRUE. The directory will always be copied to new_path, even
if the name differs from the basename of path.
translation.example:
file_create("foo")
file_copy("foo", "bar")
try:
    file_copy("foo", "bar")
except FsError as error:
    print(error)
file_copy("foo", "bar", overwrite=True)
file_delete(["foo", "bar"])
dir_create("foo")
files = file_create(["foo/bar", "foo/baz"])
show(file_exists(files))
dir_copy("foo", "foo2")
show(file_exists(path("foo2", path_file(files))))
link_create(path_abs("foo"), "loo")
show(link_path("loo"))
link_copy("loo", "loo2")
show(link_path("loo2"))
dir_delete(["foo", "foo2"])
link_delete(["loo", "loo2"])
